3.א: I do not know why it was necessary to write that the halakhah follows Rabba—for according to R. Yosef it is also forbidden to roll (food on sand). Bach wrote that we follow Rabba because he wondered why the Tur omitted the prohibition even during twilight; but regarding the prohibition of rolling, R. Yosef would seem stricter because of concern that one might shift soil (see Tosafot Shabbat 39a s.v. “ela”). One must say that Magen Avraham too aimed his difficulty at what the Tur omitted about prohibition during twilight—but both Bach and Magen Avraham should wonder why they prefaced “we hold like Rabba,” since even before twilight R. Yosef forbids lest one bury in hot ash (per Tosafot ibid.), and Mishnah Beitzah Rosh discusses this on chol as well; moreover the Tur did not omit this—it appears at the beginning of §257. Thus Bach and Magen Avraham should only wonder why rolling on sand was omitted—and it remains unclear why they needed to open with “we follow Rabba.”

8.ב: [Magen Avraham §26] One must say why Rav Betzalel (Rema) here ruled leniently when he himself did not do so in §253 §3—and one can answer as I emended there: there in §253 he warned not to place one’s pot on the ground while it boils—see §253 §5 and above.

12.ג: See Lechem Mishneh there, who elaborates; but according to Magen Avraham who cites Maggid Mishneh similarly for the kettle, Lechem Mishneh’s difficulty remains—why did the Gemara need to establish the mishnah like R. Shimon when even R. Yehudah would forbid a little water because of ṣiruf (joining liquids)? There is also a difficulty because explicitly in the resolution for Abaye, even for R. Yehudah a little (water) is forbidden due to ṣiruf—Shabbat 41b. This requires analysis; one must say Magen Avraham cited Maggid Mishneh for other rulings but not for the kettle—for the kettle one must say there is certainly no ṣiruf, as Maggid Mishneh himself writes there.
